I farm only 4.1 mu, and I am 73, so I will keep the plan simple, steady, and not too labor-heavy. I have farmed for 50 years, so I do not chase complicated methods. I will keep cotton as the main cash crop, because I know how to manage it and I have well irrigation. I will still plant mungbean with the cotton system because it fits my usual practice, needs less fertilizer, and helps spread risk. I will keep a smaller area of millet because it is reliable, handles local conditions well, and gives me grain even in a weaker year. I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed because I want more stable emergence and yield, but I will avoid pushing inputs too high on such a small farm. I will use moderate fertilizer, irrigate only as needed, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is necessary, because at my age I care about reducing labor, cost, and field trips while keeping a dependable harvest.
